Aminul Haque Advocate, instructed by S U Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Respondent No.1.

parties:
Shamsur Rahman, Deputy Inspector General of Prisons, Dhaka Central Jail, Dhaka ------- Appellant.
Vs.
Tahera Nargis Syed and another ------- Respondents.
full_judgment:
ATM Afzal, J.: This appeal, as of right, by the appellant, who at the relevant time was Deputy Inspector General of Prison, Dhaka Central Jail, is from Judgment and Order dated 31.5.89 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division; Dhaka in Criminal Contempt Case No. 6 of 1989 convicting the appellant for contempt of Court and sentencing him to pay a fine of Tk. 500'00 in default to suffer simple imprisonment for three (3) days. 

 2. The aforesaid case arose on an application filed by respondent No. 1 for drawing up a proceeding for contempt of court against the appellant and others including the Home Secretary alleging willful violation and disregard of the orders of the High Court Division to release the detenu, AT Kamruzzaman Syed, her husband, passed on 16.2.89 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 173 of 1988 and on 12.4.89 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 72 of 1989. 

 3. The respondent alleged that her husband was arrested on 14.11.1988 and detained under section 3(2) of the Special Powers Act, that she challenged the said detention under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 173 of 1988 and after hearing the High Court Division by order dated 16.2.1989 made the Rule absolute and directed the release of the detenu at once; that the said order was communicated on 20.2.89 to the appellant and others but a fresh order of detention passed by the Assistant Secretary (Security) of the Ministry of Home Affairs was served upon the detenu on 20.2.89 inside the jail; that the respondent again filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 72 of 1989 under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure challenging the order of detention dated 20.2.89 and a Rule was issued by the High Court Division and after hearing, the said Rule was made absolute and the detenu was directed to be released at once by order dated 12.4.89; that an advance order for release of the detenu was sent to the appellant and others by various Memos dated 15.4.89 and the order of release was received by the appellant and others on 16.4.89; that the appellant and others did not release the detenu and the respondent came to know on 18.4.89 that a fresh order of detention was served upon the detenu inside the jail on 17.4.89 purportedly under section 3(1)(a) of the aforesaid Act; that in spite of communication of the advance order of release to the appellant and others on 16.4.89; the detenu was not released intentionally and thereby they committed contempt of Court. 

 5. In obedience to the Rule, the appellant appeared and filed an affidavit. He stated that the order of release in respect of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 173 of 1988 was received by the jail authority on 20.2.89 and immediate action for release was taken by the jail authority after giving intimation to the Government over telephone. The detenu was brought to the jail gate to enable him to go out. As soon as the detenu was about to move out after release from the jail gate, another fresh order of detention dated 20.2.89 was served by Mr. Abdul Ali, Sub-Inspector of the Special Branch, Dhaka on the detenu who received it there and as such he could not go out. His name was entered in the jail register as a new entrant bearing detenu No. 183. 

 6. In respect of the order of release passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 72 of 1989 it was stated by the appellant that the advance order of release dated 15.4.89 was received by the jail authority on 16.4.89 during the lock up hour and as such no immediate action could be taken thereon. On the following day i.e. on 17.4.89 immediately after unlocking of the prison the action on the release order of the detenu was taken and the detenu was brought to the jail gate of the prison to enable him to move out. When he was about to go out after release another fresh order of detention dated 17.4.89 was served by Mr. Abdul Majid. Sub-Inspector, City Special Branch, Dhaka on the detenu who received it there and as such the detenu could not go out. 

 10. The High Court Division has given elaborate consideration to the various aspects of the case, but, strangely enough, the apology of the appellant and his seeking of mercy have not found a place in the entire consideration. While the anxiety of the High Court Division for the desideratum is appreciated and the dissertation as to performance of public duty in carrying out court's orders is appropriate, even then, it falls to be said that the findings and comments as to the failure of the appellant to release the detenu fully and in time could have been made with a little more understanding and with less punch. There has no doubt been some lapse on the part of the appellant in that the detenu was never allowed to cross the jail gate and the fresh detention orders were served inside the jail notwithstanding the order of release, "at once", passed by the High Court Division. But in the facts of the case it was perhaps not wholly correct to say that there was inordinate and unexplained delay in executing the order of the court. However, it is not necessary to say anything further because the appeal is not being pressed on merit. We have made the remarks because we are of the view that in the facts and circumstances of the case it was very necessary to take into account the fact of unconditional apology offered by the appellant, before sentencing him to pay a fine. 

 11. All that we can say now, having considered the facts of the case and the impugned judgment, is that the High Court Division ought to have considered the unconditional apology tendered by the appellant at the earliest opportunity and his plea of mercy. That having not been done, it may be fairly asked whether the appellant has been visited with punishment in fairness.
